items.title: 18.8 Stability of Complexes and Stability Constant (Kstab)

source_refs.note: Topic 18.8 with Table 18.5 and Quick Check 18.6, answered (PDF 30-31). The book's [Cu(NH3)6]2- and its 6NH3 equation are corrected to [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+; the chelate equation is given with charges. Answers need review.

blocks.text: The stability constant, Kstab, is the equilibrium constant for the formation of a complex ion from its constituent ions or molecules in a solvent. In water, water is the first ligand; a new ligand competes with it for the metal ion. For example:

The concentration of water, the solvent, stays effectively constant and is left out of the Kstab expression. Stability constants are usually given as log10 Kstab, which makes very large numbers easy to compare. The higher log10 Kstab, the more stable the complex and the further the equilibrium lies to the right; the lower it is, the less stable the complex and the more easily its ligands are displaced.

blocks.caption: Stability constants of some copper(II) complexes (book's Table 18.5)

blocks.text: Complexes of polydentate ligands have higher stability constants than those of monodentate ligands; this is the chelate effect, e.g. [Cu(H2O)6]2+ + 3en -> [Cu(en)3]2+ + 6H2O. A ligand that gives a higher Kstab can displace one that gives a lower Kstab: adding ammonia to the yellow chloride complex turns the solution deep blue, because the ammonia complex is much more stable: [CuCl4]2- + 4NH3 + 2H2O -> [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ + 4Cl-. Conversely, diluting a complex with a large amount of water can push the equilibrium back to the left, re-forming the hydrated ion.

blocks.title: The ammonia complex in Table 18.5
blocks.text: The book prints this complex as [Cu(NH3)6]2- and the displacement equation with 6NH3. The ammonia complex of copper(II) described in topic 18.7.1 is [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+, a positive ion, and the lesson uses that formula.

blocks.prompt: Write the Kstab expression for the formation of [Cu(NH3)4]2+ from [Cu(H2O)6]2+ and NH3.
blocks.explanation: For [Cu(H2O)6]2+ + 4NH3 <=> [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ + 4H2O: Kstab = [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2 2+] / ([Cu(H2O)6 2+] [NH3]^4); water is left out.

blocks.prompt: Using log10 Kstab for [CuCl4]2- (5.6) and [Cu(EDTA)]2- (18.8), explain why polydentate ligands form more stable complexes.
blocks.explanation: The EDTA complex is about 10^13 times more stable. One EDTA ion grips the metal through six donor atoms, forming rings, and it replaces six water molecules, so the number of free particles increases; this chelate effect strongly favours the complex.

blocks.prompt: Write the equation for the first step of the stepwise replacement of water by ammonia in [Cu(H2O)6]2+.

items: Kstab = equilibrium constant for forming a complex; water is omitted.
Larger log10 Kstab = more stable; the chelate effect makes EDTA (18.8) and en complexes very stable.
A ligand with higher Kstab displaces one with lower Kstab; dilution can reverse it.
